prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on your trip. Each site has strengths:

- Airbnb — best for unique stays, local hosts, private rooms or whole homes, lots of photos and host profiles, strong Host/Guest review system and protections (Superhost, Resolution Center). Good for medium-length stays and experiences; fees can be high and cancellation rules vary by host.

- Vrbo — focused on whole-home vacation rentals (good for families and groups). Listings tend to be full houses, often pet-friendly. Fees and cleaning charges vary; less “shared” space listings than Airbnb.

- Booking.com — broadest inventory (hotels, aparthotels, apartments, hostels and some vacation rentals). Great for last-minute bookings, pay-later/free-cancellation hotel options, and business travel. Often easiest to find hotels and professionally managed apartments; host interaction is sometimes minimal.

Which to pick by scenario
- Family/group whole-home stay: Vrbo or Airbnb (filter for entire home, number of bedrooms).
- Short city trip or business travel: Booking.com or Airbnb (Booking.com for hotels/professional apartments; Airbnb for neighborhoods and local host touches).
- Unique or local-style stays: Airbnb.
- Last-minute or flexible cancellation: Booking.com (many hotels offer free cancellation), or filter for flexible Airbnb listings.
- Pet-friendly or big houses: Vrbo or Airbnb (use filters).

How to find a good host — quick checklist
1. Look for reviews and read them carefully — pay attention to cleanliness, accuracy, communication, check-in, and whether past complaints repeat. Recent reviews matter most.
2. Prefer Superhosts (Airbnb) / Premier Hosts or Top Hosts (Vrbo) / properties with many consistent positive reviews (Booking.com shows overall score and guest comments).
3. Check the host profile: verified ID, response rate/time, how they describe themselves and house rules.
4. Inspect the photos and listing details — verify amenities, bed types, and the exact layout. Look at guest-uploaded photos in reviews.
5. Confirm cancellation, deposit, and damage policies — know the cleaning fee and any extra fees per guest.
6. Check the map and neighborhood: proximity to transit/attractions, safety, noise (reviews often mention noise).
7. Note the check-in process — self-check-in/lockbox vs host meet-and-greet (choose what fits your arrival).
8. Ask the host questions before booking (see template below) — gauge responsiveness and helpfulness.
9. Watch for red flags (see below).
10. Book and pay only through the platform; keep all communication and receipts on the platform.

Red flags
- Host asks you to pay off-platform.
- Listing has few or no reviews or many cancellations.
- Reviews repeatedly mention cleanliness, safety issues, or poor communication.
- Photos look stocky, inconsistent, or mismatched with the description.
- Host is evasive or very slow to respond to simple clarifying questions.

Quick message template to test a host (copy/paste and edit)
Hi — I’m [Name]. We’re planning to stay [dates], [number of guests, any children/pets]. A few quick questions: 1) Is the property exactly as pictured (any recent changes)? 2) How does check‑in work? 3) Are linens and towels provided? 4) Do you have any neighborhood/noise considerations we should know about? 5) Is the security/damage deposit refundable and how is it handled? Thanks — would appreciate a quick reply so we can book.

Money, fees and protections
- Compare total price (cleaning fee, service fee, taxes, refundable deposits). Sometimes a lower nightly rate hides a big cleaning fee.
- Airbnb has Host Guarantee and Resolution Center; Vrbo has Book with Confidence protections; Booking.com policies vary by property. Consider travel insurance for bigger trips.
- Always keep communication and payment in-platform for protection.

Practical booking tips
- Use filters for your must-haves (entire place, bedrooms, washer, kitchen, parking, pet-friendly).
- Sort by reviews and read the latest 10–20 reviews.
- For long stays, ask about discounts and monthly pricing.
- For group trips, double-check sleeping arrangements and exact bed counts.
- If you want a local host who helps, mention that in your message; if you want privacy, confirm self-check-in and no-host visits.

If you tell me: destination, dates, trip type (family, couple, business), and priorities (price, location, whole-home, pets, cancellation flexibility), I can recommend which platform to use and help screen a few listings.
